title: Kernel rollout regression — incident log and remediation notes
body:
Summary:

Quick notes from the emergent benchmarking sync following the kernel rollout (canary -> prod) on 2025-01-18. We observed a reproducible regression impacting median and tail latency for long-sequence chat workloads and a ~18% drop in sustained throughput for continuous-batching scenarios on p4d nodes. This doc captures timeline, repro steps, raw bench outputs, triage, and next actions.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2025-01-18 09:12 - Canary kernel v1.18 deployed to canary pool (auto-rollout).
- 2025-01-18 11:37 - Bench-runner v2 nightly jobs flagged p95 increase for seq_len=2048 chat tests.
- 2025-01-18 11:45 - Alert triggered: latency-anomaly-srv-prod@pager.
- 2025-01-18 12:05 - Rollback to kernel v1.17 on one node group for comparison.
- 2025-01-18 13:00 - Incident sync (notes below).

Immediate observation:
- p50 increased from 62ms -> 86ms for generation-only microbench (seq=512).
- p95 increased from 210ms -> 380ms for chat-long (seq=2048).
- Sustained throughput with continuous batching (avg batch_size 18) dropped from 320 tok/s -> 262 tok/s (~18%).
- Memory residency patterns changed: KV cache warm-up slower on v1.18, leading to more cache misses in first 20 tokens.

Repro steps (bench command used):
1) bench-runner v2 --model redwood/open-7b --kernel v1.18 --node-type p4d --seq 2048 --clients 50 --duration 10m --enable-cont-batching
2) Repeat with --kernel v1.17 to compare.
3) Capture perf counters: /proc/pid/smaps + nvprof sampling for 2 minutes after steady state.

Raw snippet (aggregated):
- v1.18 (canary): p50=86ms, p95=380ms, throughput=262 tok/s, avg_batch=17.8
- v1.17 (baseline): p50=62ms, p95=210ms, throughput=320 tok/s, avg_batch=18.2

Initial hypothesis queue (ranked by likelihood):
- Kernel change altered parallel-kv eviction timing -> more KV refills and GPU kernel restarts.
- A scheduling micro-change added a 70-100us jitter on attention kernels for longer sequences.
- Batch coalescing heuristics regress in edge cases with certain request-size distributions.

Triage notes from attendees:
- Miguel: saw higher memcpy stalls around iteration boundaries; suspects kernel-level L2 sync change.
- Priya: confirmed bench-runner traces show more frequent small CUDA stream synchronizations on v1.18.
- Evan: NVTX regions indicate attention kernel launch latency increased slightly for >1024 tokens.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Rolled back kernel to v1.17 in prod for remaining nodes (partial rollback completed by 12:35).
- Tuned bench-runner to prefer longer pre-warm phase (warmup=120s) to reduce KV cold starts for user-facing tests.
- Disabled auto-rollout for next 24h pending RCA.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Deep kernel diff + perf counters (Miguel) - ETA 2025-01-20.
- Add deterministic microbench for KV eviction pattern (Priya) - ETA 2025-01-21.
- Push small probe PR to measure attention-launch latency at various seq (Evan) - PR drafted: linked artifact - ETA 2025-01-19.
- Prepare postmortem draft and customer impact notes (Aisha) - ETA 2025-01-22.
- Add a guard in rollout pipeline to hold when p95 increases >25% vs baseline on canary (SRE lead) - ETA 2025-01-24.

Decisions made in sync:
- Stop the current kernel auto-rollout immediately until root cause identified.
- Prioritize a minimal-instrumentation probe in prod to capture KV hit rates at 1-minute resolution.
- Notify CS/AMs for accounts with tight SLOs (list to be assembled by Aisha).

Open questions:
- Are the observed differences only present on certain GPU geometry (p4d vs a100) or across all node types?
- Does model quantization or model sharding interact with the kernel change to amplify latency?
- Is there any observable impact on cost (GPU cycles) per token beyond throughput drop?

Notes / stray observations:
- A small subset (~3%) of requests hit an unexpected 5xx when the canary was live; correlated with largest sequences and coincident KV-miss spikes.
- Canary log snippets attached in linked artifacts (GH PR includes logs).

Follow-up sync: 2025-01-19 15:00 UTC (tentative). Please add items to the agenda in the Confluence page linked above.

Appendix: quick commands used by the diagnostics team:
- curl -XPOST https://api.redwood/internal/bench/start -d '{"job":"kv-warmup","duration":600}'
- ./bench-runner --profile=attention-latency --out=/tmp/att-v1-18.csv
- nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o TD 5 120

If you were in the incident channel and have notes not captured here, paste them below. This is intentionally terse — save detailed traces to the GH PR or Confluence page and reference them via linked_artifacts.
